In addition to calling on the DHS Inspector General to conduct an independent investigation of this week’s fatal shooting in Biddeford involving ICE personnel, @SenAngusKing and I are calling on the Department of Justice to coordinate with Maine state and local law enforcement throughout its investigation. The people of Maine deserve clear answers about the circumstances surrounding this shooting. Cooperation among federal, state, and local law enforcement is essential to providing those answers and giving the public greater confidence that the investigation is thorough, fair, and impartial.

Today, I joined my colleagues in the Maine delegation – @SenAngusKing, @chelliepingree, and @RepGolden – in calling for a comprehensive, transparent, and expedited investigation into the fatal shooting involving ICE personnel in Biddeford. We are also asking DHS to detail the extent to which it will collaborate with state and local agencies.

I spoke with DHS Secretary Mullin last night and urged him to cease all non-urgent vehicle stops in the wake of yesterday’s deadly Biddeford shooting. I am encouraged that the Department has agreed to do so. An impartial investigation into the shooting in Biddeford needs to proceed, as the details surrounding this tragedy are important. It is extremely unfortunate that the agent involved did not have a body-worn camera. In April, measures that I authored in the Homeland Security funding bill became law, including $20 million for expanded use of body-worn cameras, $2 million for de-escalation training, and a 17% increase in the independent Office of Inspector General’s budget to investigate matters such as this shooting. The Democratic government shutdown delayed enactment and implementation of these important safety measures. While it is clear ICE needs to improve its performance, it is important to remember that the work ICE does to protect our country goes far beyond immigration enforcement. ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) is tasked with combating cartels, human smuggling, child exploitation, forced labor, and more. Eliminating ICE would make our country less safe and endanger the lives and welfare of countless individuals.

While the investigation of the Biddeford shooting is not yet complete, it raises sufficient critical questions that I spoke with DHS Secretary Mullin last night and urged him to cease all non-urgent vehicle stops.

B000490.text: This week, the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, appeared before the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government. During the hearing, I asked the Director about how Congress can be any clearer to ensure that the Trump Administration understands that once a funding bill is signed into law, the President is not allowed to change or second-guess the spending and withhold it due to policy or political differences. That is at the heart of Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution and why Congress also passed the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, when President Nixon tried to withhold funds that were already obligated according to the law.

This week, I asked the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, to explain how poorly planned cuts to the federal workforce last year have weakened services and protections upon which Americans rely. This includes the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, which is responsible for protecting America’s agriculture from invasive species and diseases. USDA-APHIS began mounting a vigorous response to the resurgence of New World Screwworm – a deadly parasite affecting livestock – in 2024. However, in early 2025, the Administration illegally fired workers and forced others to resign, causing over 25 percent of all USDA-APHIS employees to leave. USDA’s New World Screwworm prevention, monitoring, surveillance, and control efforts were halted. USDA had approved $378 million in prevention and control funding for sterile fly facilities in 2023 and 2024, yet the money went unspent when the new administration paused funding. This is extremely concerning to our ranchers, and this outbreak could drive the price of food even higher. Unfortunately, we continue to see the fallout of the blunt and ill-considered cuts to federal workers, from the return of New World Screwworm to the United States, to farmers showing up to closed or understaffed Farm Service Agency offices, to attacks on our nuclear safety programs putting national security at risk. I will continue to hold the White House accountable, as I did this week during the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government hearing with Mr. Vought.

There are few corners of Capitol Hill where South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham wasn't known. Whether you knew him personally or simply watched him at work, he was impossible to ignore.   Lindsey was a ubiquitous presence in Washington – with few office holders as visible, quotable, or energetic as him. For more than three decades, he served throughout the House and Senate – building a reputation as a determined legislator, a media presence, and a dealmaker. From the green rooms to the global stage, Lindsey was always in the middle of the debate, making the case for what he believed in for South Carolina and the nation.   When it came to foreign affairs, Graham was an old-fashioned statesman and hawk. He believed America was a force for good in the world, and he never hesitated to confront those who threatened our interests and our allies – from Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea to terrorist organizations around the globe.   As Appropriators serving in different chambers, we worked together and shared a commitment to a strong national defense. I always appreciated his insight, his candor, and his willingness to pick up the phone to exchange ideas, discuss Oklahoma figures or issues, or strategize how we could bridge differences between the House and Senate. He was never shy about calling to seek advice, compare notes, or test his own impressions – a quality that reflected both his confidence and his respect for the views of others.   Lindsey approached public service with boundless energy, sharp wit, and genuine optimism. He loved serving in Congress, and it showed every day. He was a gifted communicator, a persuasive advocate, and someone who never lost his enthusiasm for the institution or for the work of governing.   I will miss Senator Lindsey Graham, and so will the Congress he served so faithfully. His gregarious nature always left us with points made crispy, cleanly, and with a laugh. That energy and humor certainly made him the ‘happy warrior’ of his political generation. His leadership, collegiality, and unmistakable presence will be deeply missed.

In light of the developments unveiled in the President’s address, I call upon @CIADirector Ratcliffe to immediately take decisive action to hold all those involved at the @CIA accountable for these egregious betrayals of the American people’s trust. We all can agree that bureaucrats who manipulate or conceal intelligence from the people’s elected leaders to push their preferred policies or end states cannot keep their jobs in the American people’s Intelligence Community. Those involved, and any who knew and remained silent, must be immediately removed from their positions of trust. The @HouseIntel Committee will be following up to ensure this is done.

Once again, unelected bureaucrats in the Intelligence Community manipulated and concealed intelligence to mislead the President, Congress, and the American people. They did this to make the intelligence say what they wanted it to say, instead of the facts of what we know and what we don’t know. These types of corrupt acts are what I have been fighting against for nearly 4 years. Since I became Chairman, this has been my number one priority and, thanks to the assistance of President Trump, we have been able to expose multiple such abuses leading up to tonight. Specifically: - In July 2025, I released, in coordination with then Director of National Intelligence Gabbard, the 2017 HPSCI Majority Staff report on the Russia Hoax, which showed the American people how individuals in the intelligence community manipulated and fabricated intelligence in a conspiracy against a President of the United States. - Then in June this year, following three years of my Committee investigation detailing the manipulation and concealment of intelligence by analysts on Anomalous Health Incidents (AHIs), former Director Gabbard recalled the Intelligence Community Assessments (ICAs) on AHIs, which involved similar corrupt acts. To be clear, there are great patriots working in the Intelligence Community who are dedicated to doing the right thing to uphold U.S. national security. But we learned tonight of some whose actions are an affront to the Constitution and rule of law. Their actions dishonor those serving their country honestly. I have seen far too many instances of intelligence bureaucrats who think they not only know better than the American people, but better than the Presidents the American people elect. This is unacceptable. Americans and their elected leaders must be able to trust the Intelligence Community and the intelligence they produce—it’s a Constitutional and national security imperative. To those politicians or talking heads who want the American people to ‘move on’ from 2020 and ‘stop looking back and look forward’—my response to you is we cannot go forward with an eroded, weak foundation. We must look ahead while also seeking to fully understand what went wrong and hold bad actors accountable. Telling the American people to just 'move on' is an arrogant and patronizing affront. Instead, tonight, President Trump trusted the American people with the facts, allowing them to arrive at their own conclusions. We, the American people, deserve that much. As a country, we are trying to move forward, but sometimes sunshine is the best disinfectant. Now it's time to hold people accountable, or this will keep happening. It’s not too late. I will continue working with President Trump and trusted members of his team to do just that.

For 250 years, our great experiment has faltered, flourished, evolved, and progressed. The American experience is ever-changing and as diverse as the people who call this country home. But one thing has remained constant – the idea of America has always been a beacon of hope. Protecting this country and the ideals and values it was founded on takes work. Democracy is demanding. It takes dedication and principle. And it takes the resounding belief that upholding those ideals and values is worth the fight because America is bigger than any one person. Because liberty can only truly endure when it is paired with responsibility, virtue, and a commitment to put public good ahead of personal ambition. Today, we celebrate the moment when our founding fathers openly declared that creating this country, based in liberty, was a necessity in the face of tyranny. Their legacy is that leadership requires courage when it’s difficult, integrity when no one is watching, and a willingness to put country above self. We must remember that our duty is not merely to the next election, but to the next generation. That should be the challenge for all Americans as we look forward to another 250 years. From Massachusetts, where the fight for freedom first began, I wish you a happy 4th of July. God Bless America always, God Bless all who call her home, and God Bless our courageous men and women in uniform who continue the fight for liberty today.

On Monday, our office suffered an unimaginable loss. Chris Matthews, my District Outreach and Communications Director, passed away unexpectedly. If any one of you begin to lose faith in our country, remember Chris Matthews. Remember he was without question one of the Commonwealth’s sharpest political minds – a generational talent. Remember that he was more than a Congressional aide. He took the belief that through our actions we all can bring needed change and brought it with him on many interstate bus rides to canvas distant pivotal states and to the doors of the families he inspired. Remember through his example that public service is a genuinely noble vocation. As a trusted member of our office, he helped countless veterans, families, and those who could not advocate for themselves. Those of us privileged to have worked with him for over fifteen years will remember his laugh and his wry, often biting, humor – contrasting the way things are to the way they could be. We will always remember his authentic belief that in this country, people can bring about progress and meaningful change. It was real to him and his sincerity shown through. Chris was a genuinely good person. He was family to all of us, and we are devastated by his loss, particularly at such a young age. Our thoughts and prayers are with Molly and Eli and the many who loved him. Though we wish we had more time with him, his memory will continue to give us faith that one person can significantly make better the lives of those around him.

This week, President Trump delivered a bizarre, meandering speech. It was billed to be about “election security.” However, much of the speech was a rehashing of campaign talking points and grievances. The truth is, Donald Trump has damaged election security and accessibility. His attacks on mail-in ballots and voter registration make it harder for citizens to vote, while his false claims that elections are not secure - provided without evidence - further undermine Americans’ faith in our elections. His demands that Congress pass the unpopular and democracy stifling SAVE America Act are part of this strategy. Just last week, Donald Trump fired the heads of the Election Assistance Commission. A bipartisan commission that helps states and local communities ensure safe and secure elections. Why would Trump do this months before the midterm elections? While Trump’s claims are both ridiculous and dishonest, they are also an attempt to set a pretense for him to claim that an election is invalid. It is important that we talk about his bogus claims this way so that voters are prepared when he discredits any results he doesn’t like.

F000466.text: Pearline Compton of Bristol Borough was the kind of woman every community hopes to have—someone whose faith, kindness, and quiet strength made every life she touched better. Born in Kelly, Louisiana, Pearline came to Bucks County as a young woman and built a life rooted in hard work, humility, family, and service. Over time, she became deeply woven into the fabric of our community. For more than 33 years, Pearline worked as a skilled press operator at Falls Manufacturing in Fairless Hills, and remarkably, never missed a single day of work. That tells you something about who she was. Dependable. Disciplined. Proud of honest work. Faithful in every responsibility placed before her. But Pearline’s greatest legacy was not only in the work she did. It was in the love she gave and the community she helped strengthen. In 1986, after the passing of her beloved niece, Eula Mae Hamilton, Pearline opened her heart and her home to Eula’s young daughters, Chrissandra and my dear friend, Valerie Hamilton, and raised them as her own. For those who know Chrissandra and Valerie, you know the remarkable women they became, and can see Pearline’s love, strength, and steady hand in both of them. That same heart extended far beyond her own home. Pearline poured herself into her community, supporting children, families, neighbors, and local organizations with the same devotion that defined her life. Through Children of God Educational Services, in Historic Bristol Borough, established and led by Valerie, she shared wisdom, encouragement, kindness, and love with young people and families across our community. That is what hometown heroes do. They show up. They love deeply. They serve quietly. They lift children, strengthen families, support neighbors, and leave a community better than they found it. Pearline Compton lived 94 years that way—with faith in action, love made visible, and kindness strong enough to shape generations. Please join me in extending heartfelt condolences to Chrissandra, Valerie, Pearline’s entire family, and all who were blessed to know and love her.

RT by @RepRitchie: Everyone deserves clean air and a plan that works for them. If you or someone you care for has a disability or uses medical equipment, smoke emergencies take extra preparation, and NYCEM is here to help you get ready with guidance. Here's what to know. 💙 IF YOU USE ELECTRIC MEDICAL EQUIPMENT: Ventilators, oxygen concentrators, CPAP machines, and powered mobility devices all depend on electricity. Know your backup power options now, whether that's battery backup, a charged power bank, or a plan to relocate. Contact your utility to register as a life-sustaining equipment customer so you're prioritized during outages. IF YOU HAVE A RESPIRATORY OR HEART CONDITION: Smoke affects you sooner and more severely. Stay indoors with windows closed when air quality is poor, run AC on recirculate if available, and keep your medications, inhalers, and oxygen supplies stocked and within reach. Talk to your doctor now about what to do when air quality drops, including when to adjust activity or seek care. CREATE CLEANER AIR AT HOME: Designate one room with as few windows and doors as possible as your clean-air room. A HEPA portable air cleaner helps. Avoid candles, smoking, frying, and vacuuming, which add indoor pollution. BUILD YOUR SUPPORT NETWORK: Identify at least two people who can check on you during an emergency, help you get to cleaner air, or assist with an evacuation. Share your plan, your medication list, and how your equipment works. If you rely on a home health aide or paratransit, ask your providers about their emergency procedures. PACK A GO-KIT THAT FITS YOUR NEEDS: Medications and copies of prescriptions, backup batteries and chargers for medical and mobility equipment, hearing aid batteries, glasses, communication cards or devices, comfort items, and instructions for your care that someone else could follow. STAY INFORMED YOUR WAY: Sign up for @NotifyNYC to get emergency alerts in the format that works for you, including accessible formats. Check air quality before going outside and plan around it. If you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or your equipment fails, call 911.

J000311.text: Today, we mourn the passing of United States Senator Lindsey Graham, a fierce advocate for the people of South Carolina.  May his memory be a blessing to his family and friends. Born in Upstate South Carolina, tragedy struck Lindsey early in his life.  After he graduated from high school, Lindsey’s mother and father passed away within 15 months of each other, leaving him without parents and his 13-year-old sister orphaned.  Lindsey shifted his focus to raising and caring for his sister, assuming a responsibility few can imagine at that age. The resilience and sense of duty he developed during those difficult years would come to define a lifetime of service. For 33 years, Lindsey served our Country in the United States Air Force.  He was awarded the Bronze Star for meritorious service shortly before retiring as a Colonel. For 31 years, Lindsey served in the United States Congress, and became one of the most influential lawmakers in our Country. Lindsey’s unexpected passing also affirms a profound truth: every day we live is a gift and a blessing from God.

O000177.text: The right to vote in our elections is a fundamental privilege reserved for American citizens, and we must take every necessary step to protect it. Current levels of enforcement are limited, allowing noncitizens to register to vote and participate in federal elections. Today, individuals registering to vote are largely relying on the honor system, simply checking a box on a federal registration form affirming that they are U.S. citizens. The Biden Administration’s open-border policies have only increased these risks and highlighted the need for stronger safeguards to protect the integrity of our elections. The SAVE America Act would strengthen these protections by requiring documentary proof of citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections.

K000404.text: Our veterans answered the call to serve our nation, and we have a responsibility to ensure they receive the care and support they have earned. I was proud to speak in support of H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, a bipartisan package that strengthens services for veterans nationwide. I am especially proud that the legislation includes two of my bills: H.R. 3400, the Territorial Response and Access to Veterans’ Essential Lifecare (TRAVEL) Act, and H.R. 6652, the U.S. Veterans of the Freely Associated States (U.S. Vets of the FAS) Act. Together, these measures expand access to specialized care, telehealth services, medications, and travel assistance for veterans in the U.S. territories and the Freely Associated States. Our veterans deserve nothing less than quality care, no matter where they live. I will continue working to ensure those who served our country receive the support, respect, and resources they have earned.

Our veterans answered the call to serve our nation. They deserve access to quality health care without having to leave the islands they call home. I introduced H.R. 9652, the Northern Marianas VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic Authorization Act, to authorize up to $3.7 million for the establishment of the first permanent VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic in the CNMI. This legislation is about ensuring our veterans have greater access to the care they have earned through their service while bringing critical VA health services closer to home. This is an important step forward, and I will continue working to ensure our veterans receive the support, respect, and care they deserve.
